sections.html:
College Park sits in Prince George's County, about 4 miles northeast of Washington, D.C. The University of Maryland takes up roughly 41% of the city's 5.68 square miles, and students are about 55% of residents. The 2020 count was 34,740 people and 11,539 housing units, with 16.8% of those units vacant.

That shapes nearly every sale. Many houses were built, bought or rented with the campus in mind, so a seller often has a tenant, a rental history, or a buyer pool of investors more than families. Demand also follows the academic calendar and federal hiring. A house listed in a slow month may sit longer, and a tenant whose lease ends in May or August sets a natural timing limit.

The city has more than a dozen named neighborhoods. Inside the 1945 incorporation boundary are Calvert Hills, Old Town, Lakeland, Berwyn, Branchville, Oak Springs, Daniel's Park, Hollywood and Sunnyside.

West of Baltimore Avenue are Lord Calvert Manor, College Park Woods, Crystal Springs, Acerdale (University View), Autoville, Cherry Hill and Camden. East of the CSX tracks are College Park Estates and Yarrow. Camden and Sunnyside lie outside the Capital Beltway. Name the neighborhood for buyers and say whether the house has been rented, which raises the permit questions covered next.

The combined fiscal 2026 rate for a College Park property is $1.6730 per $100 of assessed value. It includes a county rate of $0.9640, a city rate of $0.3350 and a special rate of $0.3740. The county applies a municipal tax rate differential inside incorporated towns, which lowers the county portion there.

Late balances grow by interest and penalties of 1.67% a month, and leaving them unpaid can end in a lien and a tax sale. The homestead credit limits taxable assessment growth on owner-occupied homes to 3% for FY2026, with a 10% state ceiling.

Prince George's County properties were reassessed for January 1, 2026, with a 10.3% average increase over January 1, 2023. Increases phase in evenly over three years, and decreases take effect in full in the first year.

Prince George's County charges a 1.4% transfer tax on a sale. The contract decides who pays it and how it is split with the state portion, so confirm the numbers with the title company before you sign.

sections.h2: Renting a house in College Park
sections.html:
The city runs its own occupancy permit program. Prince George's County does not license rentals inside College Park, so the county's single-family rental page points owners to the city.

Under the city code, an owner needs an occupancy permit before renting to anyone outside the immediate family.

  • The permit is issued to the owner for the structure and lasts one year, then renews each year.
  • The city inspects each unit at least once a year, and more often after a substantiated complaint.
  • Living in a unit without a valid permit is prohibited, and unpermitted properties may be placarded.
  • The permit cannot be transferred to another person or entity.

A buyer who plans to keep renting should expect to apply for a new permit. If you are a landlord selling, call the city to confirm your permit is current, whether any citations are open and whether the tenant has to be told about the sale. Overdue fees or an open placard can slow a closing.

sections.h2: What you must tell a buyer
sections.html:
If you sell a home with one to four units, state law (Real Property Code section 10-702) has you give the buyer a condition disclosure or a disclaimer, using the State Real Estate Commission's form.

The disclaimer sells the house as is, yet you must still reveal latent defects you know of that threaten health or safety. Deliver the form late and the buyer can cancel in writing within 5 days of getting it. Transfers by a fiduciary administering an estate are exempt, so an inherited house sold by a personal representative is treated differently. Ask the estate's attorney which form applies.

The September 24, 2001 F3 tornado is the storm most local sellers remember, and roofs, siding and trees are the usual repair items on houses of that era. Paint Branch and Indian Creek meet in the southeast corner of the city to form the Northeast Branch Anacostia River, so a buyer or title company may ask whether a property near a stream is in a mapped flood zone. Look up your own address on FEMA's map, since the city is not one flood zone.

If the roof or basement needs work and you do not want to pay for it before selling, an as-is sale to a cash buyer takes the repair negotiation out of the process.

You can live here without a car, and a listing should say so. The College Park, UMD Metro station runs the Green and Yellow lines, with MARC commuter trains stopping next to it. U.S. Route 1 (Baltimore Avenue) runs through the city, MD 193 and MD 431 serve it, and I-95/I-495 is reachable from North College Park.

The Purple Line light rail is under construction between New Carrollton and Bethesda, a 16-mile route with 21 stations, reported 92% complete, with five stations planned for College Park. A house near a future station may be priced with that in mind, so ask an appraiser how buyers are treating it before you set expectations.

sections.h2: Common problems for College Park sellers
sections.html:
The same problems keep showing up, and several come from the student-rental economy.

  • Tenants on a lease, and a buyer who wants vacant possession.
  • Wear from years of shared occupancy that a retail buyer will ask you to repair.
  • An occupancy permit that lapsed, or a city inspection with open items.
  • Inherited houses where the family lives elsewhere and no one has kept up the yard or roof.
  • Back taxes or a lien that must be paid from the proceeds at settlement.

A cash sale does not erase any of these, but it can change who deals with them. A cash buyer who purchases as is takes on the repair list, and you can ask whether the buyer will accept tenants in place. Before signing, get three things in writing: the closing date, who pays the county transfer tax and what stays in the house.

1. Gather the permit paperwork, the latest tax bill and any city notices.
  2. Decide whether the tenant stays or the house is delivered empty, and read the lease for notice terms.
  3. Complete the Maryland disclosure or disclaimer form.
  4. Order a payoff for any back taxes or liens.
  5. Close, with the title company paying those items from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Do I need a College Park rental permit to sell a rented house?
faqs.a: You do not need a permit to sell, but a rented house should hold a valid city occupancy permit while it is rented. The permit is not transferable, so a buyer who keeps renting applies for a new one.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax on a College Park house sale?
faqs.a: Prince George's County charges 1.4%. The contract sets who pays it and how it is split with the state portion, so confirm it with the title company.

faqs.q: What is the property tax rate in College Park?
faqs.a: The fiscal 2026 combined rate is $1.6730 per $100 of assessed value. Your own bill depends on your assessed value and any homestead credit.

faqs.q: Can I sell a College Park house with tenants in it?
faqs.a: Yes. The lease usually passes to the new owner. If the buyer wants the house empty, you will need to follow Maryland landlord-tenant rules and the lease terms.

faqs.q: Is College Park in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Parts of the area sit near Paint Branch and Indian Creek, so some properties may be mapped. Look up your address on FEMA's flood map, because the city is not one zone.
